Hazard: Finger or hand crushed in the knee-pad gap
How it happens: Knee bends 0 to 1.3 rad and the gap between thigh and shin shells closes
Numbers (screen): Knee 2:1: 760 N at 0.10 m from the axis at rated torque (76 N m); 2,280 N at peak (228 N m)
Control idea: Fixed guard or bellows over the knee gap, or keep the gap at least the finger size through the full range (ISO 13854 gives 25 mm for fingers; reviewer to confirm); nobody within reach during powered motion

Hazard: Finger caught between shin shell and foot cover
How it happens: Ankle tilts ±0.35 rad pitch, ±0.2 rad roll close to the floor
Numbers (screen): Direct drive: 400 N at 0.10 m at rated (40 N m); 1,200 N at peak (120 N m)
Control idea: Same as MP-01; charcoal gap cover that cannot close on a finger

Hazard: Hand caught between thigh shell and pelvis, or between the two thighs
How it happens: Hip roll ±0.25 rad swings the thighs toward each other; hip pitch closes thigh on belly shell
Numbers (screen): Hip roll 3:1: 1,140 N at 0.10 m at rated (114 N m); 3,420 N at peak (342 N m)
Control idea: Guard the inner-thigh and hip gaps, or keep hand clearance (ISO 13854: 100 mm, reviewer to confirm); check in CAD sweep

How it happens: A foot lands while someone stands next to the robot
Numbers (screen): Up to the robot's weight, 539.55 N, through one foot, plus landing impact
Control idea: Keep-out zone ≈4.4 × 4.3 m (Day 9 sketch); barrier; stop operator outside the zone

Hazard: Shin or foot strikes a person
Numbers (screen): Planned peak foot speed ≈0.45 m/s (0.144 m step in 0.6 s, smooth profile)
Control idea: Keep-out zone; joint speed limits in the signed limits file

How it happens: Controller, firmware or wiring fault drives a joint at full speed
Numbers (screen): No-load speed: 20.9 rad/s direct, 10.5 rad/s at 2:1, 7.0 rad/s at 3:1; leg tip at 0.86 m from the hip could reach ≈6 m/s
Control idea: Speed limits in drive firmware and the limits file; watchdog; independent e-stop contactor; mechanical end stops; first tests on a restraint

Hazard: Finger pinched when posing an arm, or arm drops if the pin is missing
How it happens: Arm moved by hand, or pin falls out during a test
Numbers (screen): Arm ≈1 kg (within M-10 2.0 kg allocation, assumed)
Control idea: Captive pin with retaining clip; pin check in every preflight

Hazard: Panels collide; cracks, sharp edges or skin pinched in a seam
How it happens: Joint motion pushes one panel into another
Numbers (screen): Shell mass 5.2 kg allocated (+1.6 kg risk)
Control idea: Swept-clearance study; rounded edges; measured gaps before fitting

Hazard: Cable snags or strains and cuts a sensor or power line
How it happens: Full joint range pulls a cable tight
Numbers (screen): Encoder loss must be detected within 100 ms (Day 216 target)
Control idea: Service loops; bend-radius check in CAD; stale-sensor detection

How it happens: Object slips off the tray or the tray tilts
Numbers (screen): From chest height ≈1.1 m (assumed) to the floor: 21.6 J; onto a catch tray 0.15 m below: 2.9 J
Control idea: Tray lip plus retaining pin; catch tray under the full travel; inert, unbreakable object; feet out of the drop zone

Hazard: Hand pinched between tray and robot chest or stand column
How it happens: Tray moves 0.10 m with someone's hand in the gap
Numbers (screen): Actuator push force is on its datasheet (often hundreds of N); held load only 24.5 N
Control idea: Pick the lowest push-force actuator that holds ≥98 N; guard or keep ≥100 mm hand gap (reviewer to confirm); limit switches; nobody in reach during cycles

How it happens: Load at 0.30 m reach, or someone leans on it
Numbers (screen): Overturning 7.35 N m from 24.5 N at 0.30 m; a 10 kg stand needs base half-width > 0.075 m before margin
Control idea: Wide base or bolted to the floor; tip-over check on the drawing

Hazard: Tray drops when power is cut
Numbers (screen): Held load 24.5 N; screen asks for ≥98 N datasheet holding force or a brake
Control idea: Holding force or brake confirmed by reviewer; power-off test

Hazard: Someone uses the robot as a handhold or support
How it happens: Pinned arms and tray look like handles
Numbers (screen): The robot is not designed to support any person (JB-R-059)
Control idea: Briefing before each test; sign on the barrier; no person contact in year one

Hazard: Robot walks with the object or still docked to the stand
Numbers (screen): 2 kg object plus stand coupling would change balance and loads
Control idea: Payload-present and support-present interlocks block walking; mode shown on screen
